title: Mitigate orphaned fallback state and cross-region retry amplification due to policy push races
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
During a capacity-driven incident on 2026-02-27 we observed a pattern where routers in some regions continued to route requests to model variants that were intentionally deprioritized. This produced two correlated failures: 1) 'orphaned' fallback state where a router retained a stale fallback mapping for minutes after the new policy was pushed, and 2) cross-region retry amplification where regional retries caused a fanout cascade leading to capacity burn in neighboring regions.

Why this matters:
- Customer-facing latency spikes and increased error rates for P0 customers during the spike.
- The invariant between policy snapshot application and local route-state invalidation is not guaranteed; that gap amplified in the presence of a rolling config push.

Root cause (short):
Policy push is implemented as an eventually-consistent broadcast. Routers apply new policy snapshots but invalidate sticky route state (variant affinity and fallback timers) asynchronously. A race between: (A) router A accepting a new policy that deprioritized variant V, (B) kube/infra turning up capacity and failing fast in A, and (C) KV cache eviction not yet propagated — allowed A to select fallback-to-V while other regions had begun routing away. Retries from client SDKs and our internal cross-region retry policy caused amplified traffic to the still-stale variant across multiple regions.

Evidence and artifacts:
- User-facing SLO alerts: Incident channel logs and PagerDuty runbook (see incident-2026-02-27).
- Correlation chart: /dashboards/routing/variant-fallback-fanout (Grafana) showing fanout at 2026-02-27T15:04Z.
- Router traces: gist with sample router traces showing stale-fallback decision (internal link): https://github.com/redwood-inference/router-traces/commit/3c1a2f
- Post-incident Slack thread and initial notes: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01INCIDENTS/p1677480000000

Decision goals for fix set:
- Eliminate window where a router can persist a fallback mapping incompatible with the canonical policy snapshot for more than 5s.
- Prevent cross-region retry amplification by adding conservative backoff and cooperative rate-limiting across regional retries.
- Keep runtime latency and cost overhead minimal (<3% additional avg RT per request) and avoid single-point synchronous blocking on policy rollout.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Ava Martinez: Triage notes — initial evidence points to race between policy broadcast and route-state invalidation. Repro steps attempted in staging (see test plan). Recommending immediate small-scope mitigations: 1) shorten policy TTL propagation, 2) add routing-level circuit breaker to stop retry fanout.

2026-03-04 - Ravi Patel: Confirmed repro in staging when simulating delayed KV eviction. Created two follow-ups: ENG-246821 (policy version monotonicity and ack protocol) and ENG-246822 (circuit breaker + inter-region retry backoff).

2026-03-05 - Jordan Kim (SRE): Deployed temporary guard: reject retries with >3 redirections within 30s at the edge. Reduced fanout in canary region. Need design for durable fix that doesn't rely on per-deployment toggles.

2026-03-07 - Design review (internal): Trade-offs discussed: synchronous apply vs eventual + stronger invariants. We prefer eventual with stronger consistency checks to avoid increase in policy rollout latency across 120+ clusters. Agreed on monotonic version + soft-compare invariant check on router apply.
2026-03-09 - Security review: No sensitive data changes; KMS/HSM not impacted. Security OK to proceed (review by Naomi Xu).

2026-03-11 - Ravi Patel: Implementation plan in progress. Key items: 1) policy push 2-phase commit (versioned announce + router ack), 2) local router invariant check that forces immediate cache invalidation if snapshot mismatch detected, 3) rate limiter shared token-bucket for cross-region retries, 4) new metrics and alerts. Draft PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/874, https://github.com/redwood-inference/router-agent/pull/223

2026-03-12 - PM check-in (Maya Singh): Prioritize ENG-246821 so we can avoid further incidents before a major customer ramp. We should schedule a canary in eu-west-1 and us-east-1 concurrently once PRs are merged.

ENG-246823: Add invariant telemetry and alert rule for stale-fallback-detections (owner: Priya Desai) - due 2026-03-15
ENG-246824: Update runbook: 'Routing fallback loop' with play-by-play mitigation steps and escalation contacts (owner: SRE team lead) - due 2026-03-14

acceptance_criteria: All routers emit 'policy_version' metric and report ack within 5s of push in 99% of cases
No stale-fallback-detection events in 24h of canary traffic under synthetic KV delays
Cross-region retry traffic reduction by >80% during simulated per-region capacity failure
New alert fires when a router serves more than 1% of requests with a fallback variant not present in the latest policy snapshot
